- When sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for 1–3 days ahead.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often over-anticipates; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 1–2 days ahead.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from neutral to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-forecast with upward bias starting from day 10–15.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons after volatility spikes; if forecast exceeds 3σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until reversion.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment <0.33 for 3+ days), model under-forecasts; add 0.5–1.5% bias to forecast for 5–10 days ahead.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply upward bias of 1–2% for next 5 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or positive.
